hypotheses.name: Structured Step-by-Step Decomposition
hypotheses.description: Breaking mathematical problems into explicitly numbered steps with clear intermediate goals. Each step should have a specific purpose (e.g., 'Step 1: Identify variables', 'Step 2: Set up equations', etc.).
hypotheses.rationale: Mathematical reasoning often fails when LLMs attempt to solve problems in one go or without clear structure. By enforcing a rigid step-by-step approach with explicit subtasks, the model might maintain better tracking of the reasoning process and reduce errors from skipping or misapplying steps.
hypotheses.testability: This can be tested by comparing performance on a standard prompt versus one that enforces the step-by-step structure with explicit subtasks for each problem type.

hypotheses.name: Self-Verification Through Alternative Methods
hypotheses.description: Instructing the LLM to solve each problem using two different methods and then compare the results to verify correctness.
hypotheses.rationale: LLMs may make calculation or reasoning errors in complex mathematics. By approaching each problem from two different angles and comparing results, the model might identify inconsistencies in its reasoning and self-correct before finalizing its answer.
hypotheses.testability: This can be tested by comparing performance on a standard prompt versus one that requires solving each problem with two different approaches and reconciling any differences.

hypotheses.name: Explicit Constraint Listing
hypotheses.description: Begin each problem by explicitly enumerating all constraints and conditions provided in the problem statement before attempting a solution.
hypotheses.rationale: LLMs sometimes miss or forget key constraints in complex problems, leading to incorrect solutions. By explicitly listing and referencing all constraints at the beginning, the model might maintain better awareness of problem boundaries and requirements throughout its reasoning process.
hypotheses.testability: This can be tested by comparing performance on a standard prompt versus one that requires listing all constraints and conditions before solving.

hypotheses.name: Unit and Dimensional Analysis Framework
hypotheses.description: Requiring the LLM to track units and dimensions throughout the calculation process, using them as a validation mechanism.
hypotheses.rationale: Tracking units and dimensions provides an additional consistency check that can catch many mathematical errors. This approach is widely used in physics and engineering to verify calculations and might help LLMs catch inconsistencies in their reasoning.
hypotheses.testability: This can be tested by comparing performance on a standard prompt versus one that requires explicit tracking and verification of units throughout the solution process.
